items.title: Google’s Pixel 11 isn’t the story; Gemini AI is
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Tech Editor joins Josh Lipton on Market Domination Overtime to discuss Google's (GOOG, GOOGL) new Pixel 11 smartphone lineup and its deeper integration of Gemini AI.

items.title: Google launches Pixel 11 smartphone line, including Pixel 11 Pro Fold, as Apple preps foldable iPhone
items.summary: Google debuted its Pixel 11 line of smartphones on Wednesday.

items.title: Microsoft Is Still Negative 1 Year Later: 76% Increase Lies Ahead According to This Analyst
items.summary: While its two biggest cloud rivals soared past the market this year, one hyperscaler kept beating earnings estimates and still watched its stock fall. Now a single analyst thinks the gap between perception and reality has grown wide enough to matter.

items.title: 1 of Wall Street’s Favorite Stocks for Long-Term Investors and 2 Facing Challenges
items.summary: Wall Street is overwhelmingly bullish on the stocks in this article, with price targets suggesting significant upside potential. However, it’s worth remembering that analysts rarely issue sell ratings, partly because their firms often seek other business from the same companies they cover.

items.title: GOOGL Stock Tops Retail Pick Over AMZN, META, MSFT For Next 12 Months – But META Leads Wall Street Upside
items.summary: Google-parent Alphabet is planning the largest percentage increase in AI spending, with 2026 capital expenditures projected at roughly $195 billion to $205 billion.

items.title: 3 Blue-Chip Stocks That Could Double by 2030
items.summary: A 16% annualized return sounds ambitious for trillion-dollar companies, yet three Nasdaq giants have the earnings architecture and AI tailwinds to make that math surprisingly plausible before the decade ends.

items.title: How the U.S. Is Trying to Copy China’s Supply Chain Playbook
items.summary: The chess game between Iran and the U.S. hit another stalemate this week.  In today’s issue I’m diving into a different geopolitical game: America’s bid to untangle its critical supply chains from China.  The U.S. is taking a cue or two from China’s strategy, but it’s having some trouble executing.

items.title: Big Tech Drives Up Credit Risk for Safe Firms With No AI Links
items.summary: As a flood of debt sales by US tech companies ripples through the credit market, it seems to be triggering an inadvertent rise in risk metrics for some of the world’s safest firms.
